rootRuling20261028.text:
## 2026-10-28 Root ruling: A2M gating mutant R6 survived (worker STOP at G-A4)
- Facts (_reports/2026-10-27/a2m-impl/HANDOFF.md, bm/built-mutants.json): built run G-A3 PASS first attempt (A1 + 12 matrix ids). R7, R8, P1, P4, P6 KILLED. R6 (runRow skips the live barrier wait) SURVIVED; it is not equivalent: accepted() returns on the actor's own reply and the watcher's public-lock frame arrives ~1 ms later, so without the barrier the live-leg scan can run before the frame arrives. Reconnect/restart legs still cover P1/P4/P6; only a live-path-only leak combined with a missing barrier would escape.
- Ruling (option A, A2F R5 precedent): accept R6 as a DISCLOSED, NON-EQUIVALENT survivor. It is a test-of-the-harness gap, not a privacy-proof gap: the shipped runner keeps the barrier, and every product mutant (P1, P4, P6) is killed. This narrows the #2345 rule "a survivor stops the unit unless shown equivalent" for R6 only. The local receipt states the race analysis and this ruling.
- No leaf edit now (it would break the frozen measuredFit bytes, force a fresh RED/GREEN, and kill R6 only probabilistically).
- CF-A2M-1: the next unit that amends the A2M harness adds a live-leg assertion that the watcher holds the public-lock frame for the declaration before the scan, and re-runs R6.
- Run P7 as a disclosure if time allows; it does not gate.
- 2026-10-28 Root: the UI agent's dev server moved to port 3600 (npm run dev chain 78576/54492/7016/66624, started 7:35 PM); old 11640 is gone. Root started _locks/heavy/a2m-concurrent-ui.ps1 (PID 83360) exempting only that chain for 2 h while 66624 lives with its original creation time; it clears ALLOW_PIDS on exit. Stop via a2m-concurrent-ui.stop after A2M heavy work.
rootRuling20261028.effect: Narrows the #2345 rule that a survivor stops the unit unless shown equivalent, for R6 only.

rootRuling20261028.correction: Root correction 2026-10-28 (carry-forward.md, section 2026-10-28 Root correction to the R6 ruling): the quoted sentence "Reconnect/restart legs still cover P1/P4/P6" overstated the evidence. P4 is observed at the reconnect leg; P1 and P6 coverage there is inferred, not run. The ruling stands; CF-A2M-1 adds R6+P1 and R6+P6 combined mutants and a tighter nested-A1 check.

survivorR6.desc: runRow skips the live barrier wait
survivorR6.raceAnalysis: accepted() resolves on the actor's own Event reply. The watcher's public-lock frame for the same declaration is delivered separately and lands about 1 ms later (evidence.jsonl of the R6 run, row matrix-Move-player-stale: actor movement_declared at 00:27:38.399Z, watcher movement_locked at 00:27:38.400Z; other rows show 1-2 ms gaps). Without the barrier the live-leg scan can run before that frame arrives and then has nothing to flag. The reconnect and restart legs rescan the full history from the start: P4 was observed killed there; P1 and P6 were killed at the live leg (a run stops at its first failure), so their reconnect/restart coverage is inferred from the shared projection code, not run (Root correction 2026-10-28, carry-forward.md). A live-path-only leak combined with a missing barrier would escape; that is a harness gap, not a privacy-proof gap, because the shipped runner keeps the barrier and every product mutant is killed.
